page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1ne.6xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 24 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at a baseline frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance is configured with 192.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 4 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, with stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25 percent, and single-threaded gzip compression landing in the bottom 10 percent. However, the dedicated 24-core architecture compensates in multi-threaded workloads. Multi-core CPU performance, Passmark CPU scores, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression all perform in the average tier. Memory bandwidth tests also show average performance, with read-only large block bandwidth reaching 96.89 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 52.55 GB/sec.

Given the high memory allocation and average multi-core processing capabilities, this instance is suited for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand extreme single-thread performance. Suitable applications include medium-sized databases, Redis caching layers, static web serving, and basic multi-threaded data processing. The lack of local storage and moderate 4 Gbps network bandwidth are key tradeoffs to consider for I/O-heavy applications.
